summary: The CLI (`stash`) now embeds, at build time, the versions of six release-train packages read from sibling workspace manifests, and `stash init` installs `@cipherstash/stack`, the integration adapter and `stash` pinned to those exact versions. The same pinning applies to install hints, `.cipherstash/context.json`'s installCommand, the native-module recovery hint and the `stash wizard` one-shot spawn. Init also reports version skew against already-installed packages and, interactively, offers to 'align' them in the same default-yes confirm. The change touches no encryption, payload or SQL code. The main release risk is a new coupling: the CLI now hard-depends on every pinned version being resolvable on npm. Changesets publishes packages independently (`fixed: []`), so a partial publish or an unpublished train member breaks `init` and `stash wizard` for that CLI release until a new release ships. A second, smaller risk is that skew alignment does not check direction, so an older CLI can offer, defaulted to yes, to downgrade a newer installed runtime. Unit tests and a build-artifact e2e test cover the logic and the embed, but I could not run them and saw no CI results. Overall impact is medium and a focused review is advised.

behaviour_changes.description: `stash init` install commands use `pkg@<embedded version>` instead of bare names, so npm dist-tags are no longer consulted. Interactive and non-interactive paths both install the pinned specs for missing packages.

The tsup build reads `version` from six workspace manifests listed in `RELEASE_TRAIN_MANIFESTS` and defines `__STASH_RUNTIME_VERSIONS__` in both bundles. A missing manifest or version fails the build, and a malformed embed throws when the module loads.

New init behaviour: installed-vs-expected version skew is warned on every path. Interactively, the install confirm (initialValue true) now also reinstalls the skewed packages at the CLI's versions. Non-interactively, nothing already installed is changed and align commands are printed.

`stash wizard` now spawns `<runner> @cipherstash/wizard@<embedded version>` rather than an unpinned `@cipherstash/wizard`. The native-module recovery hint changes from `stash@latest` to the pinned `stash` version.
Bundled agent skills (stash-cli, stash-drizzle, stash-dynamodb, stash-encryption, stash-supabase) gain notes on pinning and verifying the resolved version. These skills ship to customer repositories.

failure_scenarios.title: Pinned version not resolvable on npm breaks init and wizard for a whole CLI release
failure_scenarios.trigger: A published `stash` embeds a train package version that is not on the registry. This can happen through a partial `changeset publish` (stash publishes, a sibling fails), a train member whose current workspace version was never published (for example wizard 0.5.0-rc.1 or prisma-next 0.4.0-rc.1, which could not be checked offline), or a locally built or pre-publish CLI run against the registry.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: Versions are read from workspace manifests at build time (tsup.config.ts:33-58) and used verbatim by pinnedSpec (runtime-versions.ts:88-94). The release builds and then publishes (package.json:34). Changesets versions packages independently and does not publish atomically (.changeset/config.json fixed/linked empty). Before this change, bare names resolved to whatever dist-tag existed, so a missing version did not block install.
failure_scenarios.consequence: `npm install @cipherstash/stack-drizzle@X` (or `npx @cipherstash/wizard@Y`) fails with ETARGET/404 for every new user of that CLI version. Init reports 'Still missing' and its manual-install hints are also pinned to the missing version. Recovery needs a new publish, because npm publishes are irreversible. The failure is loud, with no data impact.

existing_verification.description: release-train.test.ts checks that every train manifest exists and has a version (source mode). runtime-versions-embed.e2e.test.ts checks that the built bundles contain the manifest versions.

missing_verification: No release-time check that every embedded version is actually published (e.g. `npm view pkg@ver` after `changeset publish`, or a smoke `stash init` against the registry).
No check that train packages not bumped in a release have their current workspace version already on npm.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Add a post-publish smoke step that runs `npm view` for each embedded spec, or a packed `stash init` in a temp project. Consider adding the train packages to a Changesets `fixed` group so they always publish together. Alternatively, fall back to the bare name or a dist-tag when the pinned install fails with ETARGET, with a warning.

failure_scenarios.title: Skew 'align' offers, defaulted to yes, to downgrade a newer installed runtime to an older CLI's versions
failure_scenarios.trigger: A user runs an older `stash init` (global install, cached npx, or a stale project-local CLI) in a project whose `@cipherstash/stack` or adapter is newer than the versions that CLI embeds.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: versionSkew flags any inequality (`installed !== expected`, install-deps.ts:74) with no ordering. With a TTY, offerAlign (line 175) adds the skewed packages to the install commands (line 216), and the confirm defaults to true (line 226). The message describes this as aligning 'to this release'.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Pressing Enter reinstalls the project's encryption client and adapter at an older version, which could reintroduce fixed bugs or mismatch the EQL/SQL bundle already installed. The prompt does show the exact commands and the change can be reverted with a reinstall. Non-interactive runs are not affected.

existing_verification.description: install-deps.test.ts covers skew warning, align with the prod/dev split, decline, the non-interactive no-mutation path and an unreadable manifest. It only covers installed versions older than expected.

missing_verification: No test where the installed version is newer than the CLI's embedded version.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Compare with semver and only offer alignment when the installed version is older, or default the confirm to false when alignment would downgrade. Otherwise, say 'downgrade' explicitly in the prompt.

recommended_controls.description: Add a post-`changeset publish` step to release.yml that runs `npm view <pkg>@<embedded version> version` for every train entry (or `stash init --yes` in a temp project) and fails loudly if any is missing.

Before merging, confirm that @cipherstash/wizard 0.5.0-rc.1, @cipherstash/prisma-next 0.4.0-rc.1 and the 1.0.0-rc.1 packages exist on npm, or will be published by the next release together with stash.
Make the align offer direction-aware (or default to No on downgrade) and add a test for installed > expected.
If a broken pin ships, publish a patch `stash` immediately. Users can work around it with manual installs of the bare package names.

The build reads each train manifest's version and defines __STASH_RUNTIME_VERSIONS__. It throws if a version is missing.

parseEmbeddedVersions throws on a malformed embed at module load. An absent embed gives an empty map, which leaves names unpinned.

The wizard spawn now uses the pinned @cipherstash/wizard spec.
The native-module rerun hint changed from stash@latest to pinnedSpec('stash').
Shipped skills were edited to document pinning and verifying versions.

No fixed or linked groups: train packages are versioned and published independently.
